title: Learned It from My Hands
note: Song 69, from the writer's idea: a displaced auto worker the day the generative robots appear; anger without cliche. Folk protest ballad in 6/8 (acoustic guitar, harmonica). Voice, tempo (dotted quarter) and mode provisional, not yet asked. The real test of the engine's 6/8 once the package passes on two spent lyrics. Not run.
sections: Verse 1
They gave us the sleeves in the spring
white mesh with a light at the wrist
said wear them the length of the shift
for safety, the turn and the twist
I wore mine for twenty-two weeks
I set every bolt like I do
a half turn, a pause, and a tap
two taps on the housing, then through
Chorus 1
It learned it from my hands
the half turn and the tap
it never asked my name
it only watched me work
it learned it from my hands
Verse 2
On Tuesday the turnstile went red
my badge gave a beep and a no
I saw through the glass to my bay
an arm moving where I would go
it set the first bolt like I do
a half turn, a pause, and a tap
two taps on the housing, then through
the line never slowed for the gap
Chorus 2
It learned it from our hands
four hundred on the line
it took the night shift first
and then it took the day
it learned it from our hands
Verse 3
Ray called about Dayton last night
I know what they're hiring to do
the same model runs in that plant
it learned from a fella like you
the one job they've got on the board
pays fourteen to wear the white sleeve
and stand there and teach the next arm
whatever we've got left to give
Bridge
I'm not gonna swing at the arm
the arm didn't sign for a thing
somebody upstairs made a call
and banked a nice bonus in spring
so Ray took the job with the sleeve
he's got the two kids and a loan
he gives it the half turn, the tap
and they'll walk him out when it's grown
Final chorus
It's learning from your hands
there's a light at your wrist
the half turn and the tap
and no one pays for that
it's learning from your hands
